tldr: vLLM announced day-0 support for NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on Oct 15, covering image, document and video input through OpenAI-compatible serving. OrcaRouter comparisons against Kimi K3 and DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision Exp followed on Oct 16.
whats_new: NVIDIA extended the Nemotron 3.5 family to speech on Oct 28 with Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and Granary v2, a promptable, adaptable multilingual transcription model.
why_it_matters: Nemotron 3.5 now spans multimodal VL and speech transcription, so one vendor family can cover document, video and audio inputs for agents; the real decision remains metered API versus self-hosted weights.

status.detail: Servable on vLLM since launch day; the family gained a multilingual transcription model on Oct 28.

beats.headline: vLLM ships day-0 support for Nemotron 3.5 Super VL
beats.summary: Multimodal serving (image, document, video) with OpenAI-compatible endpoints and multi-token prediction.

beats.headline: OrcaRouter pits it against Kimi K3 and DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision Exp
beats.summary: Three write-ups in one day, centered on metered pricing versus downloadable weights.

beats.headline: Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and Granary v2 add multilingual speech
beats.summary: NVIDIA's Hugging Face post presents a transcription model you can prompt and adapt, with the Granary v2 dataset.

open_questions: Do independent benchmarks confirm the index-point gaps OrcaRouter reports against DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision Exp?
Will other inference engines or clouds add Nemotron 3.5 Super VL beyond vLLM?
Does Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe get vLLM or other OpenAI-compatible serving support?
take_for_builders: If you run multimodal document or video agents, point an existing vLLM deployment at Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and rerun your own eval; for voice pipelines, test Transcribe on your own multilingual audio before swapping out your current ASR.
